experiments.verification_evidence: STATIC_AUDIT (no GPU, no checkpoint bytes; nothing was executed). FINDING 1 (P1, registry recording failure, NOT a paper omission): the paper DOES print an R@10 for SPRC. ICLR camera-ready Table 1, page 6, row `Ours (SPRC)`, Average R@10 column = 54.92. The registry stores `reported_r10: null` (workbench/registry/models.yaml:803) while its own `reported_score_note` (:806) quotes 54.92, i.e. the value was seen and then not recorded. FINDING 2 (P1, gate hole): with r10 null the comparator sees only r50/mean, so any produced R@10 passes; this is a live comparator-input defect, not merely a documentation gap. FINDING 3 (P2, unresolved arithmetic, now characterised exactly): printed averages are NOT the mean of the printed per-category values. python3: (49.18+55.64+59.35)/3 = 54.723333...  (printed 54.92, delta +0.197pp); (72.43+73.89+78.58)/3 = 74.966666...  (printed 74.97, consistent); (54.92+74.97)/2 = 64.945 (printed 64.85); (54.72+74.97)/2 = 64.845 -> 64.85. So the printed Avg. 64.85 is the mean of the *recomputed* per-category pair (54.72, 74.97) while the printed Average R@10 cell says 54.92. The per-category R@10 cells (49.18/55.64/59.35) are otherwise identical across Table 1, Table 5, Table 7 and Table 9, so the inconsistency is confined to the Average R@10 cell. FINDING 4: the registry's 64.85 is legitimately PAPER_REPORTED; it must not be reclassified as derived. FINDING 5: the paper never states a candidate-set construction, so `fashioniq_original_split` remains a code-derived reading of `native_protocol`, and the code's evaluator does not actually use the reference image as query context (src/validate_blip.py:198 passes reference features that blip2_qformer_cir_rerank.py:381 consumes only for `.device`). Runtime parity of any checkpoint is UNKNOWN.
experiments.verification_method: Two independent routes plus a third. (1) `pdftotext -layout /tmp/sprc_iclr.pdf` -> line 407. (2) rendered page image `pdftoppm -png -r 140 -f 6 -l 6` read visually -> same row. (3) arXiv HTML v1 (a different artifact) also contains 54.92/64.85. Cross-check by arithmetic in python3.

final_verdict: VERIFIED (paper-side metric records), with runtime parity UNKNOWN. SPRC: the paper prints R@10 54.92, R@50 74.97 and Avg. 64.85 for the FashionIQ validation set, so 64.85 is genuinely PAPER_REPORTED and the registry's `reported_r10: null` is a recording failure, not a paper omission (P1); the paper's own Average R@10 cell is internally inconsistent with its per-category cells by 0.20pp (P2). CSMCIR: identity is 'CSMCIR: CoT-Enhanced Symmetric Alignment with Memory Bank for Composed Image Retrieval', Zhipeng Qian et al., Findings of ACL 2026, pp. 4411-4424 (ACL Anthology https://aclanthology.org/2026.findings-acl.216/, DOI 10.18653/v1/2026.findings-acl.216; arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.03728 v3), and Table 1's CSMCIR(Ours) row gives 52.45/74.81 (dress), 57.70/75.76 (shirt), 61.14/80.98 (toptee), 57.07/77.27/67.17 averaged - all three registry values VERIFIED, and the registry's null paper_url/publication_year are fixable P3 defects. Neither model can be reproduced on this host and none was run: no checkpoint bytes for either, the SPRC checkpoint URL is login-walled and its class mapping unprovable, and the CSMCIR evaluator cannot import the pinned lavis.models package.
